text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- BRAZIL MONTHLY BASIC INTEREST RATE CUT TO 1.58 PCT
The Monetary Policy Committee cut the Central Bank's monthly basic interest rate to 1.58 percent for April from 1.62 percent in March. The cut was in line with market expectations.
-- BAMERINDUS MAY SELL INPACEL TO CANADA'S STERN

Financially troubled Banco Bamerindus may sell part of its control in Inpacel to the Canadian group Stern. The sale would alleviate some financial pressures on Bamerindus, but would not resolve the bank's liquidity problems.
O GLOBO
-- SOME 1.0 BLN REAIS SENT OUT OF COUNTRY IN BOND SCAM
Financial institutions linked to a state and municipal bond scandal sent at least one billion reais in illicit gains out of Brazil.
-- LAW STUDENT JAILED IN CONNECTION WITH KIDNAPPING
A law student was arrested in connection with the kidnapping of a merchant during a police operation to free the merchant.
-- DENGUE FEVER PREVALENT IN EVERY STATE
Dengue fever has broken out in every Brazilian state and authorities fear the number of cases could climb to 1.7 million.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- LAWMAKERS TO TESTIFY IN BOND SCAM
A congressional committee investigating a multi-million dollar bond scam has decided to hear testimony from all senators who approved bonds that may be related to the scandal.
-- ITALY PROSECUTING 70 PEOPLE IN PC FARIAS DRUG CASE

Italian justice officials are prosecuting 70 people believed to be involved in the same drug trafficking network that PC Farias, the late aide to former Brazilian President Fernando Collor, was alleged to have taken part in.
* Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
((--John Miller, Sao Paulo newsroom, 5511 248-5414))
